clue.text: No longer enough to show what others should do

parts.note: ex- describes something no longer so, as in a former partner
ample means plenty, enough

explanation.surface: A complaint that what once sufficed no longer serves as a lead for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A model held up for imitation is precisely a pattern of what others ought to follow.

clue.text: Bring about a result

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to cause or produce something
as a noun, the outcome or consequence of an action

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb to cause and the noun for an outcome, matching each half.

clue.text: A learner can get many grants

parts.note: L is the learner sign on a British car
lots means a great many

explanation.surface: A student driver is able to win a large number of awards.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to assign or apportion, so the verb form is a synonym of grants.

clue.text: Quiet, shy chap to turn into a violent one

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: the letters are made to turn into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A timid, quiet fellow is said to transform into a dangerous brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn into' asks for P (quiet) plus SHY CHAP TO to be rearranged; 'one' in the definition refers back to the chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a dangerous antisocial personality disorder, often violent, is the sense meant here.

clue.text: There's a moral in the thickness of thieves

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words the thickness, so in signals a run tucked within them

explanation.surface: A lesson is to be learned from the solidarity of criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle, so it stands for a single moral in this sense.

clue.text: Flourishes, as spring comes in

indicators.note: one piece comes in to the other, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: taken as written
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: Plant life thrives as springtime arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to exist in great plenty, so to thrive and multiply is the shared idea.

clue.text: Irregularities in a semolina recipe

indicators.note: a recipe mixes ingredients together, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something odd is found in a recipe for semolina pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomalies are departures from the norm, the same as irregularities.

clue.text: Bespectacled greeting in American state

annotationWithheld.why: Bespectacled greeting in American state (4): OHIO is HI inside O...O, but 'Bespectacled' must give the two O letters and signal the container at once, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: A late drink to go to one's head?

definitions.meaning: a cap worn in bed, which literally goes on the head

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bedtime drink and the cap once worn to sleep in.

clue.text: Individual copies sent up with speed

indicators.note: in a down entry a word sent up is read from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: to ape is to copy, so apes means copies
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, separate means distinct or individual, each one apart from the others.

clue.text: Work of monumental stupidity?

parts.note: an ornamental building with no purpose, erected on an estate, is a monumental work and also a word for foolishness

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a useless decorative building and plain foolishness, both covered by the clue.

clue.text: Catching the eye, perhaps, and marrying

definitions.meaning: fastening a hook into its eye on clothing, the hook-and-eye fastener
informally, getting together as a couple

explanation.definitionFit: Joining a hook to an eye and getting together as partners are both described by the phrase.

clue.text: The fisherman who does will be more pleased than the boatman

definitions.text: The fisherman who does will be more pleased than the boatman

parts.words: The fisherman who does will be more pleased than the boatman
parts.note: for a fisherman landing a crustacean is a success; for a rower the same phrase means fouling the stroke with an oar

explanation.walkthrough: In rowing the phrase means mistiming a stroke so the oar jams in the water, often tipping the rower backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing idiom for a botched stroke, which literally describes a fisherman's good catch.

clue.text: Good man has a right to take the lead

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous fellow has the proper claim to go first.
explanation.definitionFit: To star is to play the leading role in a show or film.

clue.text: Mere agents might make them

indicators.note: the letters might make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mere go-betweens are able to strike deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents negotiate deals and contracts, which are pacts settled between parties.

clue.text: Taking papers out is not an extra job

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Removing documents is a task beyond the extra duties.
explanation.walkthrough: An extra in film is a background actor with no lines, so a role with lines is not an extra's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A role with lines to say, as opposed to a silent extra, is an acting job.

clue.text: Gypsum and basalt are different

indicators.note: the letters are made different, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A geologist notes that gypsum and basalt are distinct rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-grained form of gypsum used for carving is known by this name.

clue.text: Gaffes to make behind the scenes

indicators.note: to make something from these letters means to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Blunders are made out of the audience's view.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of sight of the audience in a theatre, the wings and backstage area.

clue.text: Sally's cultivated pear tree

definitions.note: read as sally is, with the apostrophe s standing for is

indicators.note: a cultivated plant is worked on, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Sally is growing a pear tree in her garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a witty retort, and witty banter is a collection of such retorts.

clue.text: Uninhibited side-to-side movement by footballer

parts.note: a player's move from one club side to another with no fee paid, read as an unrestricted shift between sides

explanation.definitionFit: A football player's move to another club without a fee, when his contract has run out.

clue.text: Admittance for the course

definitions.meaning: right of entry, as in gaining entry to society
a dish served in a meal, the main dish in American usage

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the right of entry and a dish served at dinner.

clue.text: Part of 100-metre dash

parts.note: the short line joining 100 and metre is the dash in the printed phrase

explanation.definitionFit: The short stroke linking two words, as between 100 and metre, is this punctuation mark.

clue.text: Hits back in fight

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word backwards

parts.note: raps means hits or knocks

explanation.surface: Someone returns blows in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or fight, especially in practice.

clue.text: Notes or coins for the newsboy?

definitions.text: Notes or coins for the newsboy?

parts.words: Notes or coins for the newsboy?
parts.note: banknotes are this kind of currency, and a newspaper delivery boy is paid for his round of papers

explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes as opposed to coins, and literally the wage a newspaper round earns.

clue.text: Huge cost of electrical safety precaution

definitions.meaning: as in the phrase cost the world, a huge price
the ground connection in wiring, in British usage

explanation.walkthrough: In British English the ground wire is called by this name, and to cost the earth is to be very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet's name gives the idiom for a vast price and the British word for an electrical ground.

clue.text: Drop out of old American college

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone quits a long-established US university.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to drop it from a list.

clue.text: A highly informative device

parts.note: an instrument that tells you how high up you are, read as informative about height

explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft instrument that reports height above sea level.

clue.text: Direction from a governor that must be obeyed

definitions.text: Direction from a governor that must be obeyed

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the words governor that, so from points to letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: An official issues an order which everyone is bound to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' reads as an instruction to obey, but read whole the clue also describes the compass point a magnetic needle is bound to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal compass point is a direction in the geographical sense.

clue.text: His choice will get cross

parts.note: a voter marks the chosen candidate with an X on the ballot paper

explanation.definitionFit: A voter, who marks the chosen candidate with an X on the ballot.

clue.text: Is no longer a back number?

definitions.meaning: read literally as a statement that someone existed formerly
a person whose day is past, like an old issue of a magazine

explanation.definitionFit: A person whose fame or usefulness is over, read literally as a past tense of being.
